verdict.rationale: A dedicated Rate Limits page documents per-model requests-per-second and tokens-per-minute caps at every tier. It also gives spend-based tier thresholds ($0 to $5,000), states that exceeding any limit returns a 429 Too Many Requests error, and notes that per-team limits are viewable in the Console; the Batch API page adds that batch requests get higher rate limits. Missing for 10: detail on the 429 response shape (body, retry-after or rate-limit headers), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can read documented rate limits — requests and tokens per unit time, how tiers scale, and what a 429 looks like — before I hit them in production

citations.quote: Exceeding any limit returns a `429 Too Many Requests` error
The Batch API lets you process large volumes of requests asynchronously with reduced pricing and higher rate limits.
